documents.brief:
# The Five Outcasts — 60-second trailer

Two celebrated Heavenly Heroes cross a desert battlefield to retrieve a city woman supposedly abducted by five deformed beggars. The two squadrons lying there killed each other. Five shunned, immensely powerful outcasts have raised both companies to guard the only place society has left them. The woman crossed willingly. The heroes have been sent to enforce the city's version of her life.

This is adult, gory studio wuxia horror: practical prosthetics, thick crimson blood, cruel silk-robed authority, uncanny corpse drill, and abrupt percussion. Exactly five outcasts, two leading heroes and one adult woman. No beggar tribe, ranks, comic army or ordinary vampire invasion. The outcasts' bodies are specific and persistent, their powers terrifying, their motive defensive. The heroes' poverty disgust is the distorted viewpoint the trailer overturns.

Deliverable: exactly 60 seconds, 18 live-action source clips cut to 2–4-second beats (55 seconds), plus a five-second locally typeset title. Source generations may be ten seconds; the delivery is not 18 ten-second shots. Original fictional characters, dialogue and music. No actor likeness, film footage, licensed score or copied dialogue is required.
documents.treatment:
# Treatment

The first image is the aftermath of a war nobody won: red and indigo uniforms impaled on each other's weapons, hands still locked together in death. One dead hand tightens. A city voice calls the woman "stolen" before we have seen her. Shen and Lan, the Heavenly Heroes, advance in immaculate silk. Shen raises his cuff against the smell. Their elegance is established as a threat as much as a promise.

Beyond the field, a ruined salt shrine holds five people: Rook, Reed, Bell, Ash and Heel. Their bodies have been injured, altered or born outside the city's idea of perfection. They are not interchangeable monsters or a mass of beggars. Iron, thread, breath, bell and hide form a quiet control system. A turned ring pulls one black thread. Two ranks of dead soldiers stand, red facing indigo, then pivot outward to guard the refuge. The battle predates the outcasts; the dead are their wall, not their victims.

Shen cuts down an approaching corpse. The forearm flies through a short crimson burst. A thread retrieves the severed limb and the corpse stops at the chalk-and-salt boundary rather than pursuing him. Horror is followed by an exact limit. "We were sent for the woman," Lan says. We see Wen's free hand calmly take a drinking bowl. The heroes see captivity; the picture gives the audience agency.

Wen steps between the silks and the five: "I came here myself." Ash lowers his flute to let her speak. A match cut returns to Shen's spotless cuff, now red. "Come back," he orders, never asking. Lan's eyes shift from Wen to the puppet thread wound around Shen's sword: the living heroes are also caught in a story somebody else has written.

The final rush is three simple exchanges, not a crowd simulation: a taut thread deflects the jian; a corpse blocks the gate; Lan stops her blade a hand's breadth from Wen. Rook closes his ring. Both dead squadrons kneel inward, making a shelter around Wen and the five. The heroes stand outside it. "Then who needs rescuing?" Lan asks into the cut. Title: THE FIVE OUTCASTS. A single bell answers from black. No answer to which hero will obey the city.

documents.look-bible:
# Locked look

1970s Hong Kong studio wuxia horror on 35mm Eastmancolor: theatrical rock-and-temple sets, painted indigo night skies, hard vermilion lantern keys and cyan rim light, dense black shadows, visible film grain, slightly imperfect optical texture, practical wax prosthetics and thick crimson stage blood. Classical frontal blocking, legible full-body martial action, deliberate close-ups and restrained motivated camera moves. Unsettling, operatic and cruel, never a glossy fantasy game. Real cloth, solid props, coherent anatomy. One continuous take per source, no generated writing, no morphing bodies, no comic beggar army.

## Geography and coverage
The city lies screen left. The refuge lies screen right, beyond one chalk-and-salt line and a broken gate. Heroes approach left-to-right. Corpses face outward toward screen left when guarding. Keep camera south of this east-west axis. Reverse angles must be established by an eyeline or neutral insert; never flip actors to save a composition. The red squadron occupies the near rank and indigo the far rank, with distinct armour and wounds.

The field is dry ochre in late light, the shrine is vermilion practical light against a painted indigo exterior. Use 28/35mm for battlefield and five-person geography, 50mm for playable exchanges, 75/85mm for hands, disgust and moral reaction. A single short push-in marks Wen's statement, not every moment. Use locked cameras for supernatural movement so bodily causality reads. Dialogue is voice-over with reaction coverage. Blood stains persist. Optical texture comes from grading, not smeared moving bodies.
documents.lore-bible:
# World rules and story contract

1. Exactly five living outcasts: Rook, Reed, Bell, Ash, Heel. Each has one fixed bodily difference and a distinct prop; no regeneration or visual changing of impairments. There is no tribe, clan hierarchy, mass of beggars or comic army.
2. Shen and Lan are the two leading Heavenly Heroes, celebrated by the city but human and fallible, not literal flying gods. Their posture, cloth, vocabulary and reflexive aversion show a brutal class worldview.
3. Wen is an adult who asked Ash to guide her out of the city. The invitation was hers. She remains free to speak, walk, eat, refuse and leave. No hypnosis, hidden possession, captivity, sexual coercion or last-minute kidnapping twist may cancel this choice.
4. Red and Indigo squadrons slaughtered each other before the outcasts arrived. The introductory mutual impalement and the later opposing colours establish this visually. The outcasts neither started that battle nor murdered the soldiers to make an army.
5. Iron ring sets command; Reed's thread carries it; Bell marks boundaries; Ash's breath sustains stillness; Heel's drum sets a movement pulse. Not every power needs a demonstration. The trailer explicitly shows ring, thread and drill; never invent arbitrary magic beams to explain the rest.
6. The dead retain wounds, damaged armour and severed parts. They are visibly dead soldiers, not ordinary living soldiers, free-roaming zombies or talisman/Qing jiangshi. They can be raised and moved by the five; no effortless restoration of flesh.
7. The cordon protects the shrine and stops at the salt line. No city raid, peasant massacre or terror campaign. A guard may strike a blade away or block an intruder; it does not pursue a retreat. Their horrible necromancy is a frightening defense.
8. Do not equate bodily difference or poverty with moral corruption. Show grotesque wax, corpse wounds and heroes' disgust, then undermine that gaze with Wen's visible agency. The five may be hostile and use the dead without consent: the reversal does not make them harmless saints.
9. Shen's right cuff becomes red in s08; the stain stays through s14–s15. Cut forearm stays detached in s09. Wen's wrist cord is loose and unbound in all shots. Red/Indigo never swap colours. All characters and soldiers are adults.
10. The ending poses a choice; it does not resolve the rescue, turn Wen into a monster, cure the five or punish them for being poor. Title is editorial typography rendered locally, never model-generated writing.
documents.characters:
# Cast and locked appearances

## Shen
Shen, an adult male celebrated Heavenly Hero aged thirty, long straight black hair under a narrow silver crown, immaculate white silk swordsman robes with a silver cloud clasp, a straight silver jian in his right hand, clean-shaven angular face, imperious upright posture; his white right cuff stays blood-stained after the first sword strike.

## Lan
Lan, an adult female celebrated Heavenly Hero aged thirty, long black hair in a high crown bun with one silver pin, ivory silk fighting robes and a narrow dark blue sash, a sheathed straight sword at her left hip, composed oval face and an exacting level gaze; her movements are economical and grounded.

## Wen
Wen, an adult city woman aged twenty-eight, black hair in a plain low knot, faded pale-green travel robe with a repaired right sleeve, red city-citizen cord worn loose at her wrist, unbound hands, steady direct gaze; she stands and moves freely and is never chained, gagged or held.

## Rook
Rook, an adult male outcast aged fifty with a pronounced twisted upper back, one high shoulder, a lined watchful face, worn charcoal hemp layers and three heavy iron rings on a cord at his left wrist; he is physically powerful, moves with practiced balance and uses his right hand to turn one ring.

## Reed
Reed, an adult female outcast aged forty, healed left-arm amputation above the elbow, a scar across her left cheek, dark russet patched hemp coat, a bone thread spindle held in her right hand; she routes taut black thread through a wooden belt guide and never grows a replacement arm.

## Bell
Bell, an adult male outcast aged sixty with opaque blind eyes, scarred eyelids, a shaved head, worn smoke-grey hemp robe and a small bronze handbell; he orients his head toward sound, counts footsteps by listening and never tracks an opponent visually.

## Ash
Ash, an adult male outcast aged thirty-five with a visibly healed fused jaw and asymmetrical lower face, loose black hair, faded brown patched coat and a narrow bone flute; he invited Wen to cross the boundary at her request, his damaged jaw does not open normally and he never mouths dialogue.

## Heel
Heel, an adult male outcast aged forty with a pronounced right club foot, broad face, frayed ochre wrap coat and a small hide frame drum at his belt; he plants his adapted right foot before shifting weight onto his sound left leg, never sliding or changing his impairment.

## Red Squadron
The dead Red Squadron: adult soldiers in ruined dark-red lamellar armour, black helmets with short red tassels, blood-blackened cloth and pale corpse faces. They were killed by the Indigo Squadron before this story. Old spear wounds remain visible; black control thread knots at their wrists. Never living bandits, never Qing hopping vampires.

## Indigo Squadron
The dead Indigo Squadron: adult soldiers in broken indigo lamellar armour, black helmets with short blue tassels, blood-blackened cloth and pale corpse faces. They were killed by the Red Squadron before this story. Old sword wounds remain visible; black control thread knots at their wrists. Armour colours never swap.

## Performance and agency
Shen treats revulsion as evidence; his weapon arrives before his question. Lan begins with the same certainty but visibly hesitates when Wen contradicts the commission. Wen speaks plainly and stands by choice beside the people the heroes cannot bear to touch. Ash invited her because she asked. Rook wants solitude and will use an appalling power to keep it. Reed's bowl gesture is practical hospitality rather than sainthood. Bell listens, Heel regulates breath through the drum; no one mugs for a monster reveal.

departments.direction:
# Direction and performance

The story question changes at 34 seconds: not "can the heroes save her?" but "will they accept her answer?" s04 establishes their prejudiced gaze; s11 and s12 contradict the abduction without dialogue; s13 states her choice. Do not make Wen vacant-eyed or frightened of the five. Shen's cuff gesture is a choice, not involuntary illness. Lan's stop in s16 must be legible: decision precedes stillness. Exactly five outcasts share one establishing composition s05; later isolates must match that arrangement. Speak lines off screen over reaction shots, not simulated perfect lip sync. The last tableau gives refuge-side characters the interior and the heroes the threshold outside.
departments.camera-lighting:
# Camera and lighting

South-of-axis camera: city left, shrine right. 28mm battlefield, 35mm geography, 50mm exchanges, 85mm inserts; avoid wide-angle facial distortion being mistaken for character makeup. Shoot s03 and s17 as a compatible entrance/blocking pair. Hold horizon and lens height for s05 so exactly five bodies can be counted. One slow 20cm push during s13 emphasizes testimony. Action plates s08/s15/s16 remain side-on, with blade, hands and target visible. Vermilion lantern key from shrine right and cyan exterior rim behind corpses; expose faces without erasing black negative space. No orbit, unmotivated drone reveal, dutch-angle montage or internal cuts in one generated source.
departments.production-design:
# Production design and props

One location system: dry battlefield leads east into a broken salt-shrine gate. Near/far ranks have red/indigo pennants, mutual sword/spear kills and equally ruined armour. One broad salt line crosses the path. Shrine contains exactly five seated/standing places, one shared water bowl and no prison equipment. Reuse split lintel, crescent stone and red lantern to establish geography across reverses. Black thread is thick enough to read at normal playback, fastened to practical rings and soldier wrist knots. Bloody arm in s09 keeps the armour cuff seen in s08. Do not generate readable banners; insignia are simple red/indigo colour blocks. Title is created in post.
departments.costume-makeup:
# Costume, makeup and practical gore

Heroes start with immaculate white/ivory silk; a right-cuff blood stain transfers in s08 and persists. Wen's travel robe is worn, repaired and freely belted; wrists never tied. Five outcasts have individually fixed prosthetics: Rook twisted upper back, Reed healed left-arm absence, Bell opaque eyes, Ash fused lower jaw, Heel right club foot. Frame and costume distinguish them without adding horns or demon skin. Use waxen corpse appliances, painted wounds, breakaway rubber forearm and a short thick crimson blood burst. No real footage, medical demonstration or anatomical lingering. Damage belongs principally to the already-dead soldiers; do not substitute violence against the woman for horror. Practical cloth/wax remains material, not melting AI edges.
departments.choreography:
# Fight and supernatural movement

One exchange per generation. s08: corpse forearm extends from right; Shen's blade cuts left-to-right; arm drops and cuff stains; a clear held end pose. s15: same screen direction, Reed's tension redirects the point downward into stone; no sword teleport or extra hands. s16: Lan advances one step, then deliberately arrests her blade before Wen, feet planted, no contact. s17 guard moves across gate then stops on salt, never charging through it. s07: two dead ranks lift/pivot in one commanded drill, no hopping-vampire rule from the old film. Supernatural strength is communicated through stillness and precise exertion, not clutter. s18 kneeling is one unison movement that forms a barrier, with all five and Wen behind it; nobody transforms or disappears.
departments.sound-music:
# Sound and music

Five motifs: ring click, taut thread creak, bronze bell, one breathy bone-flute note, low hand drum. Introduce separately; do not layer all five continuously. Dry battlefield starts nearly silent. Armour pulse begins at s07, blade impact at s08 has no heroic fanfare. Silence before Wen's line reverses the trailer's authority. Original voice-over: envoy line over battlefield, Shen over cuff inserts, Lan over decision coverage, Wen over her free stance, Rook over final shelter. Build 48kHz stereo stems: voices, percussion, ambience, discrete impacts. Duck music beneath words; peak below -1 dBTP. Caption from the actual recorded lines/timings after voice generation, never invent captions from an unrecorded transcript. Single bell and final silence under the title. Native clip sound is a temp bed until approved mix.
departments.editorial:
# Editorial and post

Locked runtime 60.00 seconds at 24fps. 18 ten-second source handles yield 55 seconds of pictures; one local five-second title closes. Most edited beats are 2–4 seconds. s18 contributes two contiguous three-second handles, deliberately split to preserve short-shot editing controls; it is a six-second final tableau, not two new generations. Hard cuts, motivated by grasp, eyeline, thread tension or impact; no default crossfade and no optical-flow invention of choreography. J-cut envoy voice over s01, carry Lan's question across title entrance. Validate exact trim/frame math, source identity, source prompt hashes and output codecs before saving. Final remains unreviewed until the actual full cut is watched. Redo only named defective sources, preserve previous takes, and never fill missing shots with black placeholders presented as a finished movie.

critique:
# Development critique — before generation

The old concept had group spectacle without an ethical engine. This version has a false rescue premise, visible evidence contradicting it, and a decision left unresolved.
